summary: Theodoor Paul Galestin was a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1927–1936) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom, later serving as professor at the University of Amsterdam (1945–1957) and Leiden University (1957–1977).

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Boeckh, and Lachmann at Berlin (1843–1847) and earned his Ph.D. from Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at Berlin, Edinburgh (1861–1875), and Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Baader was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Bern and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Münster (1910–1913). He served as Privatdozent at Münster (1920) and professor at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1944).

Theodor Baunack worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leipzig under Curtius and Brockhaus (1880) and earned his Ph.D. at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (1882–1884), later teaching at Alte Nikolaischule from 1889.

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there, serving as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

Theodor Bloch was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Vienna under Windisch, Brugmann, and Bühler. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (from 1900) and was Reader at the University of Calcutta (~1908–1909).

Theodor Duka was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1843–1846) and St George's, University of London (~1850–1853). He served in the Bengal Army (1854–1874) and as Vice-President of the British and Foreign Bible Society.

Theodor Goldstücker worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg (Ph.D. 1836–1840) and Bonn, and under Burnouf in Paris. From 1851 to 1872, he served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London.

Theodor Korsch was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Petrov and Leontyev, completing his Ph.D. in 1877. He held posts at Moscow State University, Odesa University (~1877–1890), and the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages (1892).

Theodor Mommsen was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kiel University (1838–1843). He held posts at the universities of Leipzig, Zurich, and Breslau, the Prussian Academy of Sciences, and Frederick William University Berlin (1861–1885).

Theodor Nöldeke worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. After studying at Göttingen under Benfey and Ewald, he held professorships at Göttingen (1864), Kiel University (1864–1872), and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).
Theodor Schultze was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied law at Kiel University (~1843–1847) and also studied at Frederick William University Berlin.

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1872–1874), and Oxford under Max Müller. He taught at the University of Greifswald before becoming professor of comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).
Theodor von Oppolzer studied at the University of Vienna from ~1859 to 1865 and subsequently held an academic post there from ~1866 to 1886.

Theodore Dwight Woolsey was a linguist who studied at Yale University and Princeton University. He served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and later was president of the American Oriental Society (~1872–1887).

Theodore Riccardi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1974–1976 and 1990) and served as guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society (attested 1989).

Theodore Riccardi Jr. is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He held a faculty position at Columbia University, where he was attested as faculty in 2014 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

Theodore Stcherbatsky was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Minaev, Bühler, and Jacobi. He was attested as a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences between 1927 and 1931.
Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen was a scholar of religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Groningen from 1941 to 1956 and at Utrecht University from 1956 to 1969.
Theodorus Willem Juynboll was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University (~1886–1893) under Hendrik Arent Hamaker and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.
